## Absorb the guessed-qname failure mode instead of punishing it:… — 2026-07-30 (parent 5f67561c3276)

**Added fuzzy did-you-mean recovery for mistyped qnames on patch/batch_patch, demoted --gone to a secondary hint, and made record_intent and patch_apply_cmd report uncovered symbols even with an empty patch queue.**

Three related gaps in the patch workflow are closed together.

**Guessed-qname recovery.** A new `_close_qname_suggestions` helper (in `trie/cli`) runs rapidfuzz against `store.all_qualified_names()` and returns up to _n_ candidates. `patch_create_cmd` now calls it on `KeyError` and leads the error output with those candidates; `--gone` is demoted to a footnote for genuine removals. The same did-you-mean list is surfaced in `TrieTools.patch` (with the closest match pre-filling the fix hint) and per-item in `TrieTools.batch_patch`.

**Empty-queue coverage.** `record_intent` no longer short-circuits when `total == 0`. A new `_coverage_report` helper (extracted from the sealed path) runs `intent_gate.evaluate` and returns `{"uncovered": [...]}` or `{}`, never raises, and is now shared by both the zero-queue and normal-apply paths. `patch_apply_cmd` mirrors this: zero recorded applies fall through to the coverage report instead of returning early.

New regression tests pin both behaviours:
- `test_patch_create_suggests_close_qnames_on_miss` (in `tests/test_gate`)
- `test_record_intent_empty_queue_still_reports_uncovered` (in `tests/test_intent_gate`)
